messages:
sophia (pm): quick sync — we need to decide sequencing for the Q2 experiments bundle. customer-driven asks + cost optimizations are both high priority. thoughts on using RICE vs simple impact/effort tradeoffs?

mike (eng): my vote is RICE for cross-team clarity, but keep it lightweight. we can compute reach + confidence fast. effort estimates should come from eng leads.

chris (data): agree on RICE. also add a required metric per experiment (primary KPI) so we can A/B and measure regressions. will need baseline pulls from analytics.

anna (product ops): can we cap the initial canary to 1% and define automatic rollback thresholds? customers are sensitive.

.sophia (pm): yes — proposed rollout plan: canary 1% (24h), ramp to 10% (48h), 50% (72h), then full. gating: latency p95 backstop, error rate, quality regression on prompt set.

mike (eng): sounds good. suggest we also include a cheap model fallback route for high latency moments to avoid user-visible timeouts.

chris (data): what about statistical power for small effect sizes at 1% canary? we might not detect subtle quality drops early. consider synthetic evals + continuous scoring on canary traffic.

anna (product ops): agree — add synthetic eval + golden prompt set run every 6h against canary. if quality delta > 2% -> alert and rollback.

rollout-bot: deploy queued: experiment/priority-sequencing-v1 scheduled at 2026-04-02T09:00Z.

eva (sre): add error budget gating. if any SLO burn > 25% in 1h window during canary, auto-fallback to last stable variant. also need runbook updated.

mike (eng): here's a minimal rollout config I suggest:

```
canary:
  initial_percent: 1
  steps: [10, 50, 100]
  metrics:
    - name: p95_latency_ms
      threshold: 1.25x
    - name: request_error_rate
      threshold: 0.01
    - name: quality_delta
      threshold: -0.02
auto_rollback: true
fallback_variant: stable-v3
```

sophia (pm): love it. for prioritization, proposed RICE quick table: Reach(weekly calls), Impact(est. net retention), Confidence(data/experts), Effort(eng-weeks). we can rank and then overlay risk (infra/rollback complexity).

mike (eng): can we surface infra cost delta per experiment? Redwood Optimize suggestions could help estimate token/cost impact before rollout.

chris (data): will pull baseline metrics and run power analysis. expect a note by EOD tomorrow with minimum detectable effect at each traffic level.

anna (product ops): I'll draft launch criteria checklist: product acceptance, data readiness, SLO gates, runbook, support rotation, rollback test. will post PR to the experiments repo.

eva (sre): support rotation: include oncall + eng lead for first 48h of ramp. confirm we have dashboards for canary traffic filtered by variant.

mike (eng): one tradeoff callout — smaller canary reduces blast radius but increases time-to-detect. need to balance with customer impact risk.

sophia (pm): decision proposal: use RICE to order initiatives, but for sequencing of rollouts prefer a hybrid: conservative canaries for high-risk infra/latency changes, faster ramps for pure-product tweaks with synthetic validation.

chris (data): +1. will annotate each experiment with risk tag (latency, correctness, cost) so sequencing algorithm can prioritize low-risk quick wins.

anna (product ops): I'll add a column in the tracker: risk_tag, rollout_plan, primary_kpi, required_analyses, and a final go/no-go checklist link.

rollout-bot: note: experiment/priority-sequencing-v1 requires manual approval after data readiness check.

mike (eng): next step: eng leads to give effort estimates by EOD Tuesday, data to provide power analysis, ops to create checklist PR. then we compute RICE and publish sequencing.

sophia (pm): perfect. linking internal doc: https://redwood.internal/roadmap/experiments — everyone, please add notes in there. :sparkles:

eva (sre): small nit — ensure we have emergency kill switch in control plane for private deployments as well. customers running private might not accept auto-rollbacks without notice.

anna (product ops): noted — private customers: manual rollback unless contract says otherwise. will flag in tracker.

mike (eng): ack.

chris (data): will follow up with the statistical assumptions in the doc thread.

sophia (pm): thanks all — we'll reconvene after the estimates. short and actionable. :thumbsup:
